chunks: And (remember) Dhu'n-Noon (Jonah), when he went away in anger and imagined that We would not test him (with distress). He called out from the darkness: 'There is no god other than You. All glory to You; surely I was a sinner.'

key_terms.الظُّلُمَاتِ: The darknesses (plural), referring to the layers of darkness surrounding Jonah
key_terms.ذُو النُّونِ: Dhu'n-Noon, meaning 'the man of the fish' or 'the one with the fish', a title for Prophet Jonah

ai.seo_question: What was the supplication of Prophet Jonah (AS) from the darkness of the fish?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights Prophet Jonah’s (AS) initial impatience and premature departure as a minor error of judgment rather than a major sin, emphasizing his subsequent sincere repentance. The phrase 'in the darknesses' (az-zulumat) is interpreted by scholars like Al-Tabarsi to refer to the layers of the fish, the sea, and the night, symbolizing the trials of the soul. This narrative serves as a paradigm for believers, illustrating that turning to God in times of distress with the declaration 'La ilaha illa anta' leads to divine deliverance.
